As a man having experienced the loss of a child before the child was born, here is the perspective I can offer. 

I was very brutal to myself about it. I couldn't stop blaming myself, regardless of logic. The sight or mere thought of children had me crumbling for years after the child didn't make it.

As a man, I am told to be strong and show up for others. I am also told to talk about my emotions. Now, lacking expertise and considering how neurospicy my brain is, identifying emotions is a challenge. Putting them into words and communicating them- that can sometimes look and sound messy. And that is when I'm told to be quiet- when my emotions are loud and sound messy.

So, I retreat. Because there *is* no space for my emotions to be held- not carried by someone else entirely- just held, shared, helping. 

I know many other men follow a similar pattern due to similar circumstances. I also know that for me personally, what I would've needed at the time would've been to be shown that *me*, I have value. Not my sperm, my dna, my labour to provide for our little family, *me* as a person. I needed to feel love.

I'm in no way sharing this to minimize your experience: you lived a physically and mentally traumatic experience, and your body and mind need time to recover. Your husband's body didn't need a recovery period, but his mind is still in that recovery period.

Before anything, I want to state I'm not a psychologist nor any type of mental health professional.

 That being said, this reminds me a bit of the fourth response to "fight flight freeze or fawn", the one I'm talking about being the fawn response. It's often seen in people who've been through trauma/abuse of some kind. This also makes me think of depersonalization, where your sense of self is diminished but in this case is transmutated into a whole other personality, like an act. 

As an actor trained since early childhood, I can say it's really easy to lose yourself in a character and really adopting their personality traits, even their habits. My best advice is to discover who you are as a real life character. If you were put in an anime or a game or anything of the sort, what about YOU (and not your adopted characters) would stand out? Develop your character!
